hints: Put one node on team A. Where are all its neighbours forced to go? And their neighbours?

Two-colouring with BFS/DFS: give a start node colour 0, every neighbour the opposite colour. If you ever see an edge whose ends share a colour, it is impossible. Restart from every uncoloured node because the graph may be disconnected.

1. color[] filled with -1.
  2. For each uncoloured node s: colour it 0 and push it.
  3. Pop v; for each neighbour u: if uncoloured, give it 1 - color[v] and push; if color[u] == color[v], return false.
  4. Return true at the end.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every assignment of nodes to two teams and check all edges.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: BFS colouring; each node and edge is checked once, and a colour clash proves an odd cycle.

explain: In [[1,3],[0,2],[1,3],[0,2]], node 0 gets colour 0, nodes 1 and 3 get colour 1, and node 2 gets colour 0. Every edge joins different colours, so the answer is true. In the triangle [[1,2],[0,2],[0,1]], nodes 1 and 2 both get colour 1 but are joined by an edge, so the answer is false. An odd cycle is exactly what makes a split impossible.
recognize: Split nodes into two groups so every edge crosses between them → bipartite check by 2-colouring.
